sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
I'm Roman Mars.
The most popular sport in the world has been relatively slow to catch on here in the United
sentences.zh: 世界上最受欢迎的运动在美国一直难以流行起来，

sentences.en: States.
There's this episode of The Simpsons that I think captures the disdain with which
sentences.zh: 《辛普森一家》里有一集，我觉得捕捉到了

sentences.en: some Americans regard the rest of humanity's favorite game.
sentences.zh: 一些美国人对这项全世界最受欢迎运动的鄙夷态度。

sentences.en: It starts with the family
watching TV.
For some soccer!
The Canonical Soccer Association is coming to Springfield.
sentences.zh: 正统足球协会要来斯普林菲尔德了。

sentences.en: It's all here.
Fast kicking,
low scoring, and ties.
You bet!
Hey Dad, how come you never taken us to see a soccer game?
sentences.zh: 嘿，老爸，你怎么从来不带我们去看足球赛？

sentences.en: I don't know.
So the Simpsons decide to go to the game.
sentences.zh: 于是辛普森一家决定去看比赛。

sentences.en: And the stands are packed.
But the fans' enthusiasm
quickly evaporates as the game gets going.
sentences.zh: 球迷们的热情很快就消散了。

sentences.en: Halfback passes to the center.
Back to the wing.
Back to the center.
Center holds it.
Holds it.
Holds it.
Boring!
Come on, you snorers!
Do something!
I think it's fair to say that Homer and Krusty the Clown are echoing a common complaint about
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以说，荷马和库斯提小丑道出了美国人对足球

sentences.en: soccer that you hear in the United States a lot.
That it's not exciting enough.
That's producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 这是制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: They don't score enough points, lament these narrow-minded touchdown lovers.
sentences.zh: 这些思想狭隘的达阵爱好者抱怨说，足球进球太少。

sentences.en: I completely disagree with this perspective.
sentences.zh: 我完全不同意这种观点。

sentences.en: But even I have to admit that soccer can be a
sentences.zh: 但即使是我也不得不承认，足球确实可能是一场

sentences.en: low-scoring affair.
Professional teams routinely win games one to nothing.
sentences.zh: 职业球队经常以一比零赢下比赛。

sentences.en: Or worse yet, battle for
90 minutes and settle for a 0-0 draw.
But whatever your feelings about the relative excitement of the
sentences.zh: 但无论你对这项“美丽运动”的刺激程度有何感受，

sentences.en: beautiful game, soccer was undoubtedly more boring 30 years ago.
The world was in general agreement that the game was too slow.
sentences.zh: 当时全世界普遍认为比赛节奏太慢。

sentences.en: And it needed to be made more dynamic.
sentences.zh: 需要让它变得更具活力。

sentences.en: This is soccer writer, or football writer, Adam Hurry.
sentences.zh: 这位是足球作家亚当·赫里。

sentences.en: And Adam says that the main culprit
sentences.zh: 亚当说，导致比赛节奏变慢的罪魁祸首

sentences.en: slowing the game down was the goalkeeper.
So the goalkeeper became very useful in controlling the pace of the game.
sentences.zh: 守门员在控制比赛节奏方面变得非常“有用”。

sentences.en: Basically, teams would score a goal or two.
sentences.zh: 基本上，球队进了一两个球后，

sentences.en: And then they would do anything they could just to
kill time and protect the lead.
sentences.zh: 拖延时间，保住领先优势。

sentences.en: And the easiest way to do that was just to pass the ball to the
sentences.zh: 而最简单的方法就是把球传给

sentences.en: goalkeeper.
Who, back then, could just pick the ball up and run a few seconds off the clock before
sentences.zh: 那时候，守门员可以直接抱起球，在开球前消耗几秒钟时间，

sentences.en: throwing it back into play.
And you could do this as many times as you wanted.
sentences.zh: 而且你想做多少次都可以。

sentences.en: It kind of resulted in real sort of almost comical scenarios where they would kick the ball back to
sentences.zh: 这导致了一些近乎滑稽的场景：他们会从中场线，或者在对方半场获得任意球时，把球踢回给

sentences.en: the goalkeeper from the halfway line, from free kicks that they had in the opposition half.
Just because they knew that that would waste precious seconds, the opposition team simply
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为他们知道这样可以浪费宝贵的秒数，而对方球队根本

sentences.en: couldn't have the ball.
People finally got fed up with this uninspiring tactic during the 1990 World Cup in Italy.
sentences.zh: 人们终于在1990年意大利世界杯期间对这种毫无激情的战术感到厌倦了。

sentences.en: Now, nostalgia kind of paints the World Cup of 1990 as a wonderful tournament.
sentences.zh: 现在，怀旧滤镜把1990年世界杯描绘成了一场精彩的赛事。

sentences.en: But at the time,
it was regarded as kind of the paragon of cynical football.
sentences.zh: 它被视为愤世嫉俗足球的典范。

sentences.en: Lots of low-scoring games, lots of passing the ball back to the keeper, lots of time-wasting.
sentences.zh: 大量的低比分比赛，大量的回传给门将，大量的时间浪费。

sentences.en: There is one story about a game at Italia 90 between Egypt and Republic of Ireland,
sentences.zh: 有一个关于1990年意大利世界杯埃及对阵爱尔兰比赛的故事，

sentences.en: Ireland, where someone totaled up the amount of time that Irish goalkeeper Pat Bonner had the ball
sentences.zh: 有人统计了爱尔兰门将帕特·邦纳手持球的时间，

sentences.en: in his hands, and it added up to six minutes.
In other words, fans spent about 7% of the game watching the goalkeeper just hold the ball.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，球迷们花了大约7%的比赛时间看着守门员抱球。

sentences.en: Seth Blatter, who was the general secretary of FIFA at the time, he said this is not why people go to
sentences.zh: 时任国际足联秘书长的塞普·布拉特说，这不是人们来看

sentences.en: watch football.
It's one of the rare things he did get right in his time at FIFA.
sentences.zh: 这是他在国际足联任职期间为数不多做对的事情之一。

sentences.en: But he was spot on.
sentences.zh: 但他当时说得非常准确。

sentences.en: He was absolutely right.
This is not entertaining football.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是精彩的足球。

sentences.en: This does not inspire people.
And there is no skill in simply standing there, holding the ball in one's hands.
sentences.zh: 而且仅仅站在那里，手里抱着球，没有任何技术含量。

sentences.en: Something had to be done.
And so in 1992, the International Football Association Board,
sentences.zh: 于是，1992年，国际足球协会理事会，

sentences.en: the committee in charge of determining the rules of soccer, made a minor change to the laws of the
sentences.zh: 那个负责制定足球规则的委员会，对比赛规则

sentences.en: game.
From that season forward, in every league throughout the world, if a player intentionally
sentences.zh: 从那个赛季开始，全世界的每一个联赛中，如果球员故意

sentences.en: kicked the ball back to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper could no longer use their hands.
sentences.zh: 将球踢回给守门员，守门员就不能再用手接球。

sentences.en: So any deliberate pass back to the goalkeeper from any place on the pitch
sentences.zh: 所以，从球场任何位置故意回传给守门员的球，

sentences.en: could not be picked up.
FIFA put out a press release about the new rule, where they came down really hard on the goalkeepers.
sentences.zh: 国际足联发布了一份关于新规则的新闻稿，对守门员的态度非常强硬。

sentences.en: It was entitled, Goalkeepers are not above the law.
sentences.zh: 标题是《守门员并非凌驾于法律之上》。

sentences.en: And they were very strong about this.
sentences.zh: 他们对此态度非常坚决。

sentences.en: They
said the goalkeeper has a very rare privilege in football, the use of his hands.
sentences.zh: 说，守门员在足球运动中拥有一种非常罕见的特权，即使用手。

sentences.en: But it is a
privilege that should not be abused.
Time wasting is one of the worst forms of unsporting
sentences.zh: 拖延时间是最恶劣的非体育道德

sentences.en: behavior, because it attempts to deny opponents a fair chance of using the full allotted time
sentences.zh: 行为之一，因为它试图剥夺对手公平利用全部比赛时间

sentences.en: to use their skills to win the game.
sentences.zh: 发挥技能赢得比赛的机会。

sentences.en: The backpass law might seem like a pretty subtle tweak to the rules of soccer.
sentences.zh: 回传规则看起来像是对足球规则的一个微小调整。

sentences.en: But over time,
it would completely transform the game in ways that FIFA could never have envisioned.
sentences.zh: 它以国际足联从未预料到的方式彻底改变了这项运动。

sentences.en: This
little rule change would become one of the most consequential in the history of the sport and force
sentences.zh: 小小的规则变动成为了这项运动史上影响最深远的规则之一，并迫使

sentences.en: nearly every player on the field to adapt.
sentences.zh: 场上几乎每一名球员做出调整。

sentences.en: But in the short term, the rule change would cause
sentences.zh: 但在短期内，这一规则变动导致

sentences.en: an existential crisis for one player in particular, the goalkeeper.
sentences.zh: 某类球员陷入了生存危机，那就是守门员。

sentences.en: The goalkeeper has always been a unique specialist position, like a field goal kicker in American
sentences.zh: 守门员一直是一个独特的专业位置，就像美式足球中的踢球手

sentences.en: football or a coxswain in rowing.
They even wear a different colored shirt from their teammates,
sentences.zh: 他们甚至穿着与队友颜色不同的球衣，

sentences.en: as if to signify, I am not like the rest of you.
sentences.zh: 仿佛在宣告：我与你们其他人不同。

sentences.en: The most obvious difference is that they're allowed to do something that no one else on the field can,
sentences.zh: 最明显的区别是，他们被允许做场上其他人不能做的事，

sentences.en: touch the ball with their hands.
Goalkeepers have this strange superpower,
sentences.zh: 守门员拥有这种奇怪的超能力，

sentences.en: which they use to ruin everyone else's fun.
sentences.zh: 他们用它来破坏其他所有人的乐趣。

sentences.en: Soccer is the most popular sport in the world, and what most people love about it is the goals.
sentences.zh: 足球是世界上最受欢迎的运动，而大多数人热爱它是因为进球。

sentences.en: And it's actually our ambition to prevent goals from happening,
sentences.zh: 而我们的目标恰恰是阻止进球发生，

sentences.en: so we're sort of trying to disappoint the entire world.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是在试图让全世界感到失望。

sentences.en: This is Justin Bryant, a former professional fun ruiner,
sentences.zh: 这位是贾斯汀·布莱恩特，一位前职业“乐趣破坏者”，

sentences.en: who is currently the goalkeeping coach for the North Carolina State women's soccer team.
sentences.zh: 目前是北卡罗来纳州立大学女子足球队的守门员教练。

sentences.en: Bryant is from the United States, but he played professionally in England in the 80s and 90s
sentences.zh: 布莱恩特来自美国，但在80和90年代曾在英国职业联赛踢球，

sentences.en: for a really small club called Borumwood FC.
sentences.zh: 效力于一家名为博勒姆伍德FC的小俱乐部。

sentences.en: They paid me, I think, 50 pounds a week, plus room and board.
sentences.zh: 他们每周付给我50英镑，外加食宿。

sentences.en: And so, by the slimmest of margins, I made a living, but I did.
sentences.zh: 所以，我勉强维持了生计，但我确实做到了。

sentences.en: Justin was this kid from Florida, living out of a bed and breakfast, trying to follow his dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀是个来自佛罗里达的孩子，住在民宿里，努力追逐他的梦想。

sentences.en: But it wasn't always easy.
sentences.zh: 但这并不总是那么容易。

sentences.en: The fields were in bad shape.
Fans were sometimes hostile.
And the style of play in England at the time wasn't very sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 而且当时英国的比赛风格并不太讲究技术。

sentences.en: Teams would just kick these long balls forward
sentences.zh: 球队只会把球长传向前，

sentences.en: and hope that their big, bruising striker would make something happen.
sentences.zh: 希望他们那个身材魁梧的前锋能创造出什么机会。

sentences.en: You know, I had to very quickly get used to balls being played into the box
sentences.zh: 你知道，我必须很快适应球被吊入禁区，

sentences.en: and three or four great, big, bald-headed, tattooed guys
sentences.zh: 三四个高大、秃头、满身纹身的家伙

sentences.en: flying in, trying to run me over, essentially.
sentences.zh: 冲过来，本质上是想把我撞倒。

sentences.en: But it's the goalkeeper's job to go grab that ball, no matter what.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，守门员的工作就是去抓住那个球。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's actually counter to several million years of human evolution,
sentences.zh: 是的，这实际上违背了数百万年的人类进化规律，

sentences.en: throwing ourselves, hurling ourselves in front of a ball that's moving at a high rate of speed.
sentences.zh: 我们要把自己投掷出去，挡在高速移动的球前面。

sentences.en: Some people say you have to be crazy to be a goalkeeper.
sentences.zh: 有人说当守门员必须得疯。

sentences.en: Justin doesn't love that word,
but he says that goalkeepers are just wired a little bit differently than everybody else.
sentences.zh: 但他认为守门员的思维方式确实与众不同。

sentences.en: If he spots a soccer team at the airport, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果他在机场看到一支足球队，

sentences.en: he can recognize the goalkeeper right away.
sentences.zh: 他一眼就能认出谁是守门员。

sentences.en: It's a different personality type.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不同的人格类型。

sentences.en: It's a different mindset, a different mentality.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不同的思维方式，一种不同的心态。

sentences.en: They carry themselves differently.
They express themselves differently.
sentences.zh: 他们的表达方式也不同。

sentences.en: What are the telltale signs of a goalkeeper?
sentences.zh: 守门员有什么明显的特征吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
Goalkeepers tend to have kind of a knowing smirk.
sentences.zh: 守门员往往有一种心照不宣的坏笑。

sentences.en: That's the best way I'd put it.
sentences.zh: 这是我能想到的最好的形容方式。

sentences.en: It's almost like they're saying, yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 就好像他们在说，没错，我懂。

sentences.en: I know what you think, but I still like to do this.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在想什么，但我还是喜欢这样做。

sentences.en: I grew up playing soccer, and I never wanted to be the goalkeeper,
sentences.zh: 我从小踢足球，但我从来不想当守门员，

sentences.en: in part because it felt like such a thankless job.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为这感觉是一份吃力不讨好的工作。

sentences.en: When goalies do everything right, they get taken for granted.
sentences.zh: 当守门员表现完美时，他们会被视为理所当然。

sentences.en: But if they make one mistake, everyone notices.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们犯了一个错，所有人都会注意到。

sentences.en: We can make utter fools of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会让自己出尽洋相。

sentences.en: We can make just the most horrific mistakes that lose games.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会犯下极其可怕的错误，导致球队输掉比赛。

sentences.en: And it's very evident to everybody watching when that happens.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，所有观众都看得一清二楚。

sentences.en: What a fatal error!
What on earth is he doing?
But what happened to the goalkeeper?
sentences.zh: 但守门员发生了什么事？

sentences.en: I think that's every goalkeeper's nightmare,
sentences.zh: 我想那是每个守门员的噩梦，

sentences.en: where you have nothing to do the whole game,
sentences.zh: 整场比赛都没什么事可做，

sentences.en: and then the other team gets one chance,
sentences.zh: 然后对方球队获得了一次机会，

sentences.en: and it squirms right under your hands and into the goal,
sentences.zh: 球从你的手下溜进球门，

sentences.en: and you lose by that goal.
sentences.zh: 而你因为这一个球输掉了比赛。

sentences.en: Whoops-a-daisy!
Oh, they misjudged it!
That has to be the worst mistake that I have ever seen
sentences.zh: 这一定是我见过的最糟糕的失误，

sentences.en: from an excellent goalkeeper!
sentences.zh: 出自一位优秀的守门员之手！

sentences.en: That's a recipe for a sleepless night or two.
sentences.zh: 这足以让人失眠一两个晚上了。

sentences.en: For that reason, the goalkeeper developed a reputation
sentences.zh: 正因如此，守门员逐渐有了名声，

sentences.en: as kind of a lonely outsider.
sentences.zh: 被视为一种孤独的局外人。

sentences.en: French existentialist philosopher Albert Camus was a goalkeeper,
sentences.zh: 法国存在主义哲学家阿尔贝·加缪曾是一名守门员，

sentences.en: if that tells you anything.
sentences.zh: 如果这能说明什么的话。

sentences.en: You know, obviously I've been around goalkeepers now
sentences.zh: 你知道，显然我作为守门员这个职业，

sentences.en: as my profession for a quarter century,
sentences.zh: 已经有四分之一个世纪了，

sentences.en: and there were a lot of individualists, iconoclasts, loners,
sentences.zh: 那里有很多个人主义者、反传统者、独行侠，

sentences.en: whatever you want to call them.
We are kind of alone,
tasked with keeping the ball out of the net with our hands.
sentences.zh: 任务就是用双手把球挡在球门外。

sentences.en: For Justin Bryant's whole life,
sentences.zh: 在贾斯汀·布莱恩特的一生中，

sentences.en: that had been his one job,
to keep the ball out of the net with his hands.
sentences.zh: 用双手把球挡在球门外。

sentences.en: That is, until 1992.
I didn't hear about it until it actually did happen.
sentences.zh: 直到事情真正发生，我才听说。

sentences.en: Like, it just, I think anecdotally somebody mentioned,
sentences.zh: 就像，我想只是有人随口提了一句，

sentences.en: oh, starting next season you can't pick up a back pass.
sentences.zh: 噢，下赛季开始你不能再用手接回传球了。

sentences.en: And I just couldn't, I couldn't believe it
because there were an awful lot of goalkeepers
sentences.zh: 因为有太多太多的守门员，

sentences.en: that weren't suited for it at all.
Goalkeepers in England were trained in how to block shots,
sentences.zh: 英国的守门员受训内容是封堵射门、

sentences.en: catch crosses, and fight for loose balls.
sentences.zh: 接传中球，以及争抢松散球。

sentences.en: All things you mostly do with your hands.
sentences.zh: 这些大多都是用手完成的动作。

sentences.en: A training session in the old days,
a goalkeeper session in the 1980s,
wouldn't involve playing the ball with your feet at all,
at no point.
But now, if someone on their own team passed them the ball,
sentences.zh: 但现在，如果队友把球传给他们，

sentences.en: the goalkeeper would be stripped of their superpowers.
sentences.zh: 守门员就会被剥夺他们的“超能力”。

sentences.en: They would need to use their feet,
just like everybody else.
And that turned out to be a bit of a problem
because a lot of them just didn't know how.
sentences.zh: 因为他们中很多人根本不知道怎么做。

sentences.en: 1992 was a big year for English soccer.
sentences.zh: 1992年对英国足球来说是重要的一年。

sentences.en: It was the start of a brand new, highly commercialized league
sentences.zh: 那是一个全新的、高度商业化联赛的开端，

sentences.en: that would go on to become the most lucrative in the world,
sentences.zh: 后来成为了世界上最赚钱的联赛，

sentences.en: the English Premier League.
sentences.zh: 即英格兰足球超级联赛。

sentences.en: There were big money sponsorships and a new TV deal.
sentences.zh: 当时有大额赞助和新的电视转播协议。

sentences.en: The whole country was watching soccer.
But that first weekend of games in this critical season
sentences.zh: 但在这个关键赛季的第一个周末，

sentences.en: were pretty sloppy.
We had a weekend full of goalkeepers making horrendous errors
sentences.zh: 那个周末，守门员们犯下了骇人听闻的错误，

sentences.en: because they just didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: That's Adam Hurry again.
Goalkeepers were in a blind panic.
sentences.zh: 守门员们陷入了盲目的恐慌。

sentences.en: The ball would be kicked back to them as it used to be
sentences.zh: 球会像过去一样被回传给他们，

sentences.en: because defenders had a habit of doing that.
sentences.zh: 因为后卫们习惯那样做。

sentences.en: But then once the ball was at their feet,
they had sheer terror.
sentences.zh: 他们就感到了极度的恐惧。

sentences.en: Over the first few months,
it was as if all the goalkeepers in England
sentences.zh: 就好像英国所有的守门员，

sentences.en: were working together to collaboratively produce
one long blooper reel.
There were slips and falls and bizarre own goals.
